correctness.rationale: The 3-round Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé invariant is exactly the set of realized one-round ordered-pair atomic-extension types, since every product is vertex transitive and pairwise atomic triples exhaust the remaining 1-move possibilities. Adjacent pair common neighbors equal q_i-2; distance-two pairs have two common neighbors; distance>=3 have none. Exclusive-neighbor and shared-nonneighbor counts follow by inclusion–exclusion from N=prod q_i and Delta=sum(q_i-1). All positivity boundaries split by d=1, d=2, d>=3 and factor size two versus >=3, including F=N-2Delta=2 only at the binary 3-cube, into exactly nine distinct profile sets. Minimal products have sizes 2,3,4,6,8,9,12,16,27. Independent direct triple atomic diagrams confirmed all nine representatives, distinctness, and equivalence of (2,2,3) with (2,3,3), plus all three-factor multisets from alphabet sizes 2,3,4. Infinite classification rests on the exact general inequalities, not those examples.
